solutions.title: Change bases and simplify the sums
solutions.explanation:
Changing to a common logarithm base exposes the cancellation between the two sums. For every positive integer \(k\),
\[
\log_{5^k}3^{k^2}
=\frac{k^2\log3}{k\log5}
=k\frac{\log3}{\log5},
\]
and
\[
\log_{9^k}25^k
=\frac{2k\log5}{2k\log3}
=\frac{\log5}{\log3}.
\]
Therefore the first sum is
\[
\frac{\log3}{\log5}\sum_{k=1}^{20}k
=\frac{\log3}{\log5}\cdot\frac{20\cdot21}{2}
=210\frac{\log3}{\log5}.
\]
The second sum has \(100\) identical terms, so it equals
\[
100\frac{\log5}{\log3}.
\]
Their product is
\[
210\frac{\log3}{\log5}\cdot100\frac{\log5}{\log3}
=\boxed{21{,}000},
\]
which is choice \(\text{E}\).
